chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who kills his son: is he to be killed for him? He said: “No, and neither of the two inherits from the other if he kills him.”

key_terms.أَحَدُهُمَا: either one of the two; referring to the father and the son
key_terms.أَيُقْتَلُ بِهِ: is he killed for him; meaning whether qisas is carried out against the killer
key_terms.إِذَا قَتَلَهُ: if he kills him; the condition that causes the ruling to apply
key_terms.يَرِثُ: inherits; receives inheritance from the deceased
key_terms.يَقْتُلُ: kills; the act of intentional homicide discussed in the ruling
key_terms.ٱبْنَهُ: his son; the child in the father-son legal case
key_terms.ٱلْآخَرَ: the other; the reciprocal party in inheritance

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a father kills his son, and does either inherit from the other?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a father who kills his son. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام states that the father is not subject to retaliatory execution for that killing, and that mutual inheritance is cut off between the killer and the one killed when one of them kills the other.
